question: Are L2 regularization and weight decay equivalent for adaptive gradient methods such as Adam, and does decoupling weight decay from the gradient update improve generalization and hyperparameter separability?
hypothesis: Weight decay and learning rate can be decoupled by applying the decay outside the gradient-based update, and doing so makes Adam generalize better and compete with SGD with momentum.
contributions: Show that L2 regularization and weight decay are not equivalent for Adam (Propositions 1-3).
Propose decoupled weight decay (SGDW, AdamW) which separates the optimal weight decay from the learning rate.
Show AdamW generalizes substantially better than Adam with L2 on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32.
Propose normalized weight decay and warm restarts for Adam (AdamWR) for better anytime performance.

method.summary: Algorithms 1 and 2 move the weight decay term lambda*theta out of the gradient (so it is not rescaled by Adam's second-moment estimate) and into the parameter update, giving SGDW and AdamW. They are compared with SGD/Adam with L2 on Shake-Shake-style 26 2x64d and 26 2x96d ResNets on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32, over grids of learning rate and weight decay, three LR schedules, and 100 to 1800 epochs.

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.preprocessing: regular data augmentation procedure for the CIFAR datasets

models.name: 26 2x64d ResNet (Shake-Shake setup)
models.architecture: 3-branch residual net, depth 26, 2 residual branches, first block width 64

models.name: 26 2x96d ResNet (Shake-Shake setup)
models.architecture: as above with first block width 96

training.objective: classification loss (cross-entropy) plus L2 regularization or decoupled weight decay
training.optimizer: SGD with momentum (SGD, SGDW) and Adam (Adam, AdamW); warm-restart variants SGDWR and AdamWR
training.lr: Adam default alpha=0.001 for the 1800-epoch runs; grids of initial learning rate over powers of 2 (e.g. 1/1024 to 1/2 for SGD) in the 100-epoch runs
training.lr_schedule: fixed, step-drop (drops at epochs 30, 60, 80) and cosine annealing; cosine annealing used for the rest. Warm restarts: eta_t = 0.5+0.5cos(pi*Tcur/Ti), example T0=100, Tmult=2
training.epochs: 100 (grid and schedule comparison); 1800 (generalization runs); other budgets shown in SuppFig 3
training.weight_decay: grids of lambda; normalized weight decay lambda = lambda_norm*sqrt(b/(B*T)); best lambda_norm about 0.025 to 0.05
training.regularisation: Shake-Shake regularization from Gastaldi (2017) code base, plus L2 or decoupled weight decay

other.fig3_grid: 12 settings of L2 factor for Adam and 7 settings of normalized weight decay for AdamW, lr fixed to 0.001, 1800 epochs, 26 2x96d
other.suppfig2_grid: 4 by 4 logarithmic grid of lr and weight decay for standard Adam, 1800 epochs
other.warm_restart_Tmult: Tmult=2 example; initial Ti 1% to 10% of expected budget suggested

metrics.name: relative improvement in test error
metrics.definition: AdamW vs Adam at default lr 0.001

baselines: SGD with momentum with L2 regularization
eval.protocol: Grid search over learning rate and weight decay per schedule and budget; single reported runs in text, no seeds or error bars stated; heatmaps mark top-10 settings. Gastaldi (2017) setup.

evidence.quote: We always used a batch size of 128

results.claim: Adam with decoupled weight decay (AdamW) gives 15% relative test-error improvement over Adam with L2 at the default lr 0.001; this is Adam vs AdamW (not SGD), on a 26 2x96d Shake-Shake ResNet, 1800 epochs, and uses Top-1 error on CIFAR-10 but Top-5 on ImageNet32x32.
results.setup: 26 2x96d ResNet, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32, lr 0.001, cosine annealing, 1800 epochs, best settings of each
results.quote: For the default learning rate of 0.001, AdamW achieved 15% relative improvement in test error compared to Adam both on CIFAR-10 (also see SuppFigure 5) and ImageNet32x32 (also see SuppFigure 6).
results.note: Intro says 15% holds for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32, training budgets 100 to 1800 epochs, three schedules; actual per-cell error values are only in figures, not text. Not a result for SGD or for ResNets in general.

results.claim: Optimal weight decay and learning rate are largely decoupled with decoupled weight decay: SGDW and AdamW have a more separable hyperparameter space than L2 versions (shown qualitatively in heatmaps, no numeric measure).
results.setup: 26 2x64d ResNet CIFAR-10, 100 epochs, grid of lr and lambda
results.quote: The proposed SGDW and AdamW (right column) have a more separable hyperparameter space.
results.note: Text says 'largely decouples' and 'more separable', 'some problem-dependent implicit coupling may of course remain'; not full independence.

results.claim: With L2, Adam's best non-zero L2 results were comparable to its best with lambda=0, so Adam did not benefit from L2.
results.setup: Fig 2 bottom left, 26 2x64d ResNet CIFAR-10, 100 epochs
results.quote: Adam did not beneﬁt from it at all: its best results ob-tained for non-zero L2 regularization factors were comparable to the best ones obtained without theL2 regularization

results.claim: Decoupled weight decay outperforms L2 for all three LR schedules, with larger gaps for better schedules; cosine annealing is best.
results.quote: decoupled weight decay outperforms L2 regularization for all learning rate schedules, with larger differences for better learning rate schedules

results.claim: AdamWR sped up AdamW by up to a factor of 10 (at first restart).
results.quote: AdamWR greatly sped up AdamW on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32, up to a factor of 10 (see the results at the ﬁrst restart)

results.claim: Optimal raw weight decay shrinks as the number of epochs grows; sqrt normalization lambda=lambda_norm*sqrt(b/(BT)) makes it transfer across budgets and datasets.
results.setup: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32x32, 26 2x64d ResNet, AdamW and SGDW
results.quote: the greater the total number of epochs the smaller the values of the weight decay should be
results.note: Authors say experiments were not very comprehensive.

results.claim: Without normalization, raw lambda for ImageNet32x32 would have been roughly 5 times too large vs CIFAR-10 at the same epochs.
results.setup: ImageNet32x32 epoch is 24 times longer than CIFAR-10
results.quote: λ would have been roughly 5 times too large for ImageNet32x32

results.claim: Best normalized weight decay values were very similar across SGDW and AdamW.
Third-party: AdamW vs Adam on Deep4Net EEG, 73.68% vs 71.37% accuracy; on ResNet 72.04% vs 61.34%.
results.setup: Voelker et al. 2018 EEG data, same hyperparameters, provided privately to authors
results.quote: AdamW with the same hyperparameter setting as Adam yielded higher test set accuracy on Deep4Net (73.68% versus 71.37%) and statistically signiﬁcantly higher test set accuracy on ResNet (72.04% versus 61.34%).

results.claim: Standard Adam with L2 for 1800 epochs on a bigger net is at best comparable to AdamW at 18 times fewer epochs and smaller network.
results.quote: comparable to the ones obtained with AdamW with 18 times less epochs and a smaller network

results.claim: L2 equals weight decay for SGD only when lambda'=lambda/alpha; for Adam no L2 coefficient makes them equivalent.
results.setup: Propositions 1 and 2, proofs in App A

limits: Experiments only on image classification (CIFAR-10, ImageNet32x32) with Shake-Shake ResNets; authors say results must be verified on a wider range of tasks.
Belief that results hold for AdaGrad and AMSGrad is untested.
Square root normalization is based on few experiments; authors say better rules likely exist.
No seeds, error bars, hardware or compute reported; per-run errors only in figures.
Language-model use (Radford et al. 2018) only cited, not tested here.
The 15% figure compares Adam vs AdamW only; AdamW closed most but not all of the gap to SGDWR on CIFAR-10.

terms.definition: theta_{t+1} = (1-lambda) theta_t - alpha grad f_t(theta_t), decay applied separately from the gradient step (Eq 1)
lambda = lambda_norm*sqrt(b/(B*T)), b batch size, B training points, T epochs
